To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
“Statistical models for metaphor processing can be successfully trained with little or no human annotation and can generalize across languages.

1) weakly supervised and fully unsupervised methods are effective for metaphor processing; 2) the type of supervision is language-specific; and 3) the type of clustering (flat vs. hierarchical) is also language-specific

(1) the best performing models for metaphor processing require only a few annotated examples and can be applied to data in different languages; (2) the models can be used in cross-linguistically valid ways; and (3) the models are capable of learning higher-level mechanisms of conceptual metaphor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing and testing statistical models of metaphor processing that are robust and scalable across languages and domains.
two important questions in computational metaphor processing: (1) How to learn metaphor from text? And (2) how to scale metaphor learning?
the development and application of weakly supervised, unsupervised and cross-lingual techniques for metaphor processing.
